entries.verification_note: pub fn, unique name in the whole crate (`rg -n "compare_mean_time\(" src/` returns only these 3 call sites plus the declaration). Two calls are inside compute_relative_speeds (one direct at line 36, one inside a sort_unstable_by closure at line 79) so that enclosing symbol appears twice, matching how corbel emits one caller row per resolved reference rather than deduplicating by enclosing symbol.
Private (non-pub) fn. `rg -n "compute_relative_speeds\(" src/` returns exactly the declaration plus these 3 call sites, all in the same file as the definition.

pub fn. Three same-file callers use the bare identifier `fastest_of(...)`. The fourth, real caller at scheduler.rs:75 calls it as `relative_speed::fastest_of(&self.results)` - a module-path-qualified call. corbel's Rust reference_query (crates/corbel-lang/src/langs/rust.rs REFERENCE_QUERY) only captures `call_expression` nodes whose `function` is a plain `(identifier)` or a `(field_expression)`; a `function: (scoped_identifier)` node like `relative_speed::fastest_of` matches neither pattern and produces no relationship row at all. corbel is therefore structurally blind to this caller (a guaranteed false negative), while grep/ripgrep find it immediately by text. This mirrors an identical structural gap independently found in corbel's own repository (see corbel.json's tsx.rs -> typescript::is_public case).

Same structural gap as hyperfine-03: scheduler.rs:77 calls `relative_speed::compute_with_check_from_reference(...)`, a scoped_identifier call invisible to corbel's Rust reference_query. The only caller corbel can in principle resolve is the in-file test at line 167.

Private fn, unique name in the crate. Both callers are in the same file as the definition, calling it as a bare identifier (not through the Executor trait), so this is unambiguous despite being adjacent to the dynamic-dispatch case below.

`run_command_and_measure` is a required method of the `Executor` trait (declared, bodyless, at executor.rs:37) with 3 concrete implementations: RawExecutor (line 133), ShellExecutor (line 186, this entry), and MockExecutor (line 323). Exactly one call site is statically provable to target ShellExecutor's implementation specifically: executor.rs:251, inside `impl Executor for ShellExecutor`'s own calibrate method, where `self` has concrete type `&mut ShellExecutor` so Rust resolves the call at compile time with no ambiguity. Four further textual occurrences of `.run_command_and_measure(` exist at src/benchmark/mod.rs:64,215,247,309, all calling through `Benchmark.executor: &'a dyn Executor` (mod.rs:38, a trait object) - genuine runtime dynamic dispatch with no way to prove statically (from source alone) which of the 3 impls actually executes for a given hyperfine invocation. Those 4 sites are intentionally excluded from verified_callers; a tool that reports them as callers of ShellExecutor::run_command_and_measure specifically is scored as a false positive, since the same 4 sites are equally plausible callers of RawExecutor's or MockExecutor's implementations and no static ground truth singles out ShellExecutor.

ground_truth.name: table_header
ground_truth.note: self.table_header(&cells_alignment) at markup.rs:30, inside MarkupExporter's own default table_results method body. 3 types implement MarkupExporter: AsciidocExporter overrides table_header with its own implementation (asciidoc.rs:8); OrgmodeExporter and MarkdownExporter define no override and fall through to this same trait's default table_header (markup.rs:87). Which one executes for a given self.table_header() call depends on the concrete Self behind the generic/trait-bound call at markup.rs:30, not determinable from that call site's source text alone.

verification.verification_note: ADVERSARIAL. Discovered during hand-verification of table_header (markup.rs:87, the trait's own default implementation), not flagged by the mechanical scanner. rust-analyzer's references for table_header@markup.rs:87 return 3 hits: markup.rs:30 (the real, but ambiguous, self.table_header() call inside table_results - this entry), asciidoc.rs:8 (AsciidocExporter's own override *signature*, which rust-analyzer surfaces as a trait-impl relationship, not a call - verified by reading asciidoc.rs:7-9: `impl MarkupExporter for AsciidocExporter { fn table_header(...) {...} }` has no call expression at that line), and asciidoc.rs:63 (a test, `exporter.table_header(...)` where `exporter: AsciidocExporter`, which statically resolves to AsciidocExporter's own override at asciidoc.rs:8, not to this trait-default candidate - a second false attribution). After discarding both non-callers, the only genuine call reaching this specific default implementation (rather than a concrete override) is markup.rs:30, and even that call is not staticaly resolvable to this one function versus AsciidocExporter's override, since MarkupExporter::table_results is itself a default method invoked generically across all 3 implementors. This entry is framed as an ambiguous-callee task on table_results (the caller) rather than a caller-list task on table_header (the callee), matching the shape of corbel-05 and itsdangerous-03.
